claim:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $e$ be a nilpotent endomorphism of a
finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, let
$G_e=\{g\in\mathrm{GL}(V):geg^{-1}=e\}$ be its centralizer, and let $d\ge0$.

1. Every $G_e$-fixed endomorphism $B\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V^{\otimes d})$
   is the value at $e$ of a $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-equivariant polynomial map
   $\Phi\colon\operatorname{End}(V)\to\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes d})$
   (polynomial in the matrix entries of the input, with
   $\Phi(gXg^{-1})=(g^{\otimes d})\Phi(X)(g^{-1})^{\otimes d}$).
2. Every such equivariant polynomial map is a finite sum
   $\Phi(X)=\sum_hc_h\,\sigma_h(X^{h_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes X^{h_d})$ with
   $h_i\ge0$, where $\sigma_h$ is a place permutation of the $d$ tensor
   factors and $c_h$ is an invariant scalar polynomial in $X$ (a polynomial
   in the traces $\operatorname{tr}(X^k)$).

The extension in (1) is proved by Hartogs lifting on the normal codimension-$\ge2$
orbit closure; the structure in (2) is proved by polarization and the
Schur-Weyl description of tensor invariants, not by importing a
first-fundamental-theorem for the full matrix algebra.

[F1] $X$ is the spectrum of a reduced irreducible normal domain $A=\mathbb C[X]$, and $O$ is its dense open orbit; $G_e$ is the unit group of the full finite-dimensional associative centralizer algebra $C_e=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C[e]}(V)=\{b:be=eb\}$. Its units are exactly $\{b\in C_e:\det b\ne0\}$: if $b$ commutes with $e$ and is invertible on $V$, its inverse also commutes with $e$. This is a nonempty open subset of the affine vector space $C_e$, containing the identity, so $G_e$ is smooth, irreducible and connected; no product-of-matrix-algebras identification is needed ([[lem-type-a-nilpotent-orbit-closures-are-normal-via-chain-varieties]], [[def-nilpotent-endomorphism]], [[thm-nilpotent-jordan-string-basis]]).

1.1 Hartogs lifting. Let $A=\mathbb C[X]$ and let $f\in\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ be regular on $O$, hence regular off a closed subset of $X\setminus O$; since $\partial X$ has codimension $\ge2$ in $X$ by the normality lemma [F1], $f$ is regular in codimension $1$ and therefore extends to $A$ by [F2]. Applying this coordinatewise to maps into a finite-dimensional vector space shows that every regular map $O\to W$ into a finite-dimensional vector space extends uniquely to a regular map $X\to W$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 The equivariant map on $O$. Fix $B\in\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes d})^{G_e}$ and define, for $g\in\mathrm{GL}(V)$, $F(g\,e\,g^{-1}):=(g^{\otimes d})\,B\,(g^{-1})^{\otimes d}\in\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes d})$. This is well defined: if $g_1e g_1^{-1}=g_2eg_2^{-1}$, then $g_2^{-1}g_1\in G_e$, so $(g_2^{-1}g_1)^{\otimes d}B(g_2^{-1}g_1)^{-\otimes d}=B$ by $G_e$-invariance, which rearranges to $(g_1^{\otimes d})B(g_1^{-1})^{\otimes d}=(g_2^{\otimes d})B(g_2^{-1})^{\otimes d}$. The map $F$ is $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-equivariant by construction: $F(hXh^{-1})=(h^{\otimes d})F(X)(h^{-1})^{\otimes d}$ for $X\in O$. [F1, construct, algebra]

2.1 Regularity of $F$ on $O$. The ranks of $X^0,X^1,\dots,X^{l-1}$ are constant on $O$. Cover $O$ by open charts where fixed minors used to select bases of the kernels and images, their quotient complements and Jordan top vectors are nonzero. Gaussian elimination on such a chart gives a Jordan basis for $X$ with entries regular in $X$. Let $g(X)$ carry a fixed Jordan basis for $e$ to this chosen Jordan basis for $X$, with the same ordered string lengths. Then $g(X)e g(X)^{-1}=X$. Restricting to the open chart where the Jordan-basis determinant is nonzero makes both $g(X)$ and $g(X)^{-1}$ regular, since their entries have only the fixed nonvanishing minors and determinant as denominators. Thus $X\mapsto(g(X)^{\otimes d})B(g(X)^{-1})^{\otimes d}$ is the map of step 1.2 and is regular on each chart. These charts cover $O$; on overlaps $g_2(X)^{-1}g_1(X)\in G_e$, so the expressions agree by $G_e$-invariance of $B$. Hence $F$ is regular on $O$. [F1, step 1.2, algebra, construct]

claim:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector
space, let $e\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ be nilpotent with largest
Jordan string length $l\ge1$, let $d\ge0$, and put $E=V^{\otimes d}$. Let
$$B=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$$
act on $E$ by the individual operators $x_i=e$ (in the $i$-th tensor factor)
and the place permutations, and let
$\varphi\colon U(\mathfrak g^e)\to\operatorname{End}(E)$ be the algebra map
induced by the diagonal action of $\mathfrak g^e=\{X:[X,e]=0\}$ and
$\psi\colon B\to\operatorname{End}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}$ the map encoding the
right action. Then
$$\varphi(U(\mathfrak g^e))=\operatorname{End}_B(E),\qquad \operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g^e}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}=\psi(B),$$
for every nilpotent Jordan type and every $d$. If $e$ has at least $d$ Jordan
strings of the maximum length $l$, then $\psi$ is injective. For $d=0$ the
identities are scalar identities and injectivity is automatic.

The full converse uses the proved normality and covariant-extension suppliers
of this page; it is not a stable-only claim and it does not assume the double
commutant identity.

[F3] Normality and covariants: the orbit closure of $e$ is normal with
$\operatorname{codim}\partial X\ge2$, and every $G_e$-fixed endomorphism of
$V^{\otimes d}$ is the value at $e$ of a $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-equivariant
polynomial map $\Phi(X)=\sum_hc_h(X)\sigma_h(X^{h_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes X^{h_d})$
with scalar invariant coefficients
([[lem-type-a-nilpotent-orbit-closures-are-normal-via-chain-varieties]],
[[lem-nilpotent-orbit-equivariant-tensor-covariants-extend-and-polarize]]).

1.2 The second centralizer. An operator $T$ commutes with the diagonal $A$-action if and only if it is $G_e$-fixed, because $G_e=A^\times$ generates $A$ linearly in the diagonal representation: differentiating $t\mapsto(1+ta)^{\otimes d}$ at $t=0$ recovers the diagonal action of $a$, and Newton-type generation is not needed for this direction. By [F3] every $G_e$-fixed operator is $\Phi(e)$ for an equivariant polynomial covariant $\Phi(X)=\sum_hc_h(X)\sigma_h(X^{h_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes X^{h_d})$; evaluating at $X=e$ replaces each $X^{h_i}$ by $e^{h_i}$, which is a polynomial in the individual $e$-operators of degree less than $l$, so $\Phi(e)\in\psi(B)$ (the truncated algebra $B$ contains exactly the polynomials $e^0,\dots,e^{l-1}$ in each factor and the places). Conversely every element of $\psi(B)$ commutes with the diagonal $A$-action: for $a\in A$ put $\Delta_d(a)=\sum_{k=1}^d a^{(k)}$; each individual $e^{(j)}$ satisfies $[\Delta_d(a),e^{(j)}]=[a,e]^{(j)}=0$, and each place permutation $P_\sigma$ satisfies $P_\sigma\Delta_d(a)P_\sigma^{-1}=\Delta_d(a)$. These operators generate $\psi(B)$, so their products and linear combinations also commute with every $\Delta_d(a)$. Therefore $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g^e}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}=\psi(B)$. [F3, algebra]

claim:
## Definition

Fix the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, its box-labelled natural module $V=\mathbb C^N$,
an arbitrary origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$.
Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the imported Skryabin and Vust inputs.
For $X\in\mathfrak p$ define the column-trace character
$$\kappa_c(X)=\sum_{b=1}^l c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb}),$$
where $X_{bb}$ is its $b$th column-Levi diagonal block. Write
$\eta_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ for the resulting automorphism of $U(\mathfrak p)$,
so $\eta_c(e_{a,b})=e_{a,b}+\delta_{a,b}c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}$.
Let $\mathbb C_c$ be the corresponding one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module
and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a
separate integer chain for each complex coset as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

The **truncated (deformed) tensor space** $E_c=V_c^{\otimes d}$ is
$E=V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak p)$-action obtained by composing
the ordinary total tensor representation $\rho_d$ with $\eta_c$.
Equivalently it is $\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, with one character
factor; the origin twist is applied once to the total action. For $d\ge1$
its right $H_d(\Lambda)$-action is determined by place permutations $s_i$ and
$$x_1\mapsto\Bigl(e+\sum_{j=1}^N(c_{\operatorname{col}(j)}+q_{\operatorname{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}\Bigr)\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\operatorname{col}(i)<\operatorname{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)},$$
with $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Here the generator-fixing anti-involution of
the Hecke algebra converts the displayed operators into a right action.
For $d=0$ there are no $x_j,s_i$, $H_0(\Lambda)=\mathbb C$, and $E_c=\mathbb C_c$.

Grade the box basis by $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, use the total
tensor grading and its induced endomorphism filtration, and use the fixed
loop chart $\zeta\colon\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)\to U(\mathfrak g^e)$ of
[[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]:
$\zeta(\operatorname{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$.
The coefficient index remains the actual unshifted $T=FDE$ index of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
The restricted character on the fixed centralizer basis is
$$\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c),\qquad \sigma_i(c)=\sum_{b=1}^{p_i}c_b.$$
Consequently the **full graded left representation** in this fixed chart is
$$\varphi_{d,c}(X)=\sum_{t=1}^d X^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}_E\qquad(X\in\mathfrak g^e),$$
where $X^{(t)}$ acts in tensor position $t$. In particular its complete
mode-symbol dictionary is
$$\operatorname{gr}_r\Phi_{d,c}(T_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^r\left(\sum_{t=1}^d e_{i,j;r}^{(t)}+\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c)\operatorname{id}_E\right),$$
where $\Phi_{d,c}$ is the restricted $W(\lambda)$-action. On the right,
$\operatorname{gr}_1x_j=e^{(j)}$ and $\operatorname{gr}_0s_i$ is the place
permutation. Thus the graded bimodule is the character-twisted Vust module
$\mathbb C_{\kappa_c|\mathfrak g^e}\otimes E$, with the ordinary truncated
polynomial/permutation action. It need not be the untwisted Vust module in
the fixed chart. Nevertheless its unital left image algebra and its
commutant are exactly the untwisted Vust image algebra and commutant, as
proved below.

The displayed right operators commute with $W(\lambda)$; full
$\mathfrak p$-commutation is not asserted. They make $E_c$ a filtered
$(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The actual balanced Skryabin map gives
a coherent isomorphism
$\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to E_c$ of
$(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules. For every complex origin, every pyramid and
every $d$, the two filtered image algebras are mutual centralizers, and their
associated graded image algebras are the unital Vust image algebras. No
admissibility or stable-range restriction enters this centralizer assertion.

If the pyramid is empty, $N=l=0$, use $V=0$ and $W=U(\mathfrak g^e)=\mathbb C$.
For $d=0$ all structures are scalar; for $d>0$, $E=0$ and the empty
cyclotomic product is $1$, giving the zero quotient and zero endomorphism
algebra. All formulas and centralizer identities then have these evident
empty interpretations.

$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, its box-labelled natural module $V=\mathbb C^N$,
an arbitrary origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$.
Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the imported Skryabin and Vust inputs.
For $X\in\mathfrak p$ define the column-trace character
$$\kappa_c(X)=\sum_{b=1}^l c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb}),$$
where $X_{bb}$ is its $b$th column-Levi diagonal block. Write
$\eta_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ for the resulting automorphism of $U(\mathfrak p)$,
so $\eta_c(e_{a,b})=e_{a,b}+\delta_{a,b}c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}$.
Let $\mathbb C_c$ be the corresponding one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module
and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a
separate integer chain for each complex coset as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

[F4] The cyclotomic quotient for arbitrary complex roots has its bounded monomial basis and polynomial filtration, with graded algebra $B^0=\mathbb C[X_1,\dots,X_d]/(X_1^l,\dots,X_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$; the generator-fixing anti-involution descends ([[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]).

[F5] On the untwisted tensor space $E$, the unital image $A^0=\varphi_{d,0}(U(\mathfrak g^e))$ and the operator image $D^0$ of $B^0$ are mutual centralizers for every nilpotent shape and degree, including scalar degree zero ([[thm-vust-double-centralizer-for-the-type-a-nilpotent-centralizer]]).

5.1 For $d\ge1$ and $l\ge1$, let $C_k$ be the span of tensors whose first box has column at most $k$. The preceding formula preserves every $C_k$ and gives $C_k(x_1-a_k)\subseteq C_{k-1}$. Successively applying the factors from column $l$ down to column $1$ kills $C_l=E$; they are polynomials in one operator and commute, so $\prod_{b=1}^l(x_1-a_b)=0$. This proves the quotient factorization directly for arbitrary complex origins, including repeated roots. In the total grading $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, the left-shift part has degree one; the diagonal part and each two-position exchange have total degree zero. Hence $\operatorname{gr}_1x_1=e^{(1)}$. Since the longest Jordan string has length $l$, $(e^{(1)})^k\ne0$ for $0\le k<l$ on this nonzero tensor space. A monic annihilating polynomial of degree $k<l$ would have that nonzero degree-$k$ symbol. Therefore the displayed degree-$l$ polynomial is the exact minimal polynomial, consistent with F4. [F1, F4, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 The right action is filtered with $x_j$ of degree one and places of degree zero: this holds for $x_1$ by step 5.1 and for each $x_{j+1}$ by $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Taking degree-one symbols gives $e^{(j+1)}=s_je^{(j)}s_j$; the extra $s_j$ has degree zero. By F4 the resulting graded right map is the ordinary map $X_j\mapsto e^{(j)}$, $w\mapsto P_w$ on $B^0$. Together with step 3.2 this identifies the entire graded bimodule with the character-twisted Vust module in the Definition. [F4, step 5.1, step 3.2, algebra]

7.1 Since $\tau_c$ is an automorphism, $\varphi_{d,c}(U(\mathfrak g^e))=\varphi_{d,0}(U(\mathfrak g^e))=A^0$ as unital graded subalgebras of $\operatorname{End}(E)$. Equivalently each shifted generator differs from its untwisted operator by the explicitly known scalar multiple of the identity, and either set generates the other together with the common unit. Consequently their commutants are identical as well. By F5, $A^0$ and the unchanged right image $D^0$ are mutual centralizers. This proves the required Vust comparison without identifying the two fixed-chart modules. [F5, step 2.2, step 3.2, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 Let $C=\Phi_{d,c}(W)$ and $D$ be the algebra of right Hecke operators, with filtrations induced from $\operatorname{End}(E)$. They commute by step 2.1. The symbol maps in steps 3.2 and 6.1 have images $A^0,D^0$, respectively, which are contained in $\operatorname{gr}C,\operatorname{gr}D$. For any commuting filtered operator algebras, taking the largest homogeneous terms of a commutator gives the inclusions $\operatorname{gr}C\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(D)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}D)$, where $Z$ denotes the commutant in the relevant endomorphism algebra. The same argument with $C,D$ interchanged gives $D^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}D\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(C)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}C)\subseteq Z(A^0)=D^0$. Every inclusion is equality. This also proves strict equality of the graded image algebras, rather than presuming that an arbitrary filtered representation is strict. [F5, step 2.1, step 7.1, algebra]

10.1 For $d=0$, $E_c=\mathbb C_c$, $\varphi_{0,c}(X)=\kappa_c(X)$ and $\mu_0$ is the identity; the right algebra is $\mathbb C$. Both unital operator images and commutants are scalar, even when the fixed-chart character is nonzero. For an empty pyramid the positive tensor powers are zero and both operator image algebras and both commutants in $\operatorname{End}(0)$ are zero; degree zero is scalar. Thus the exceptional cases stated in the Definition are covered without evaluating a nonexistent $x_1$ or invoking a positive-string Vust hypothesis. [F3, F4, step 1.1, step 9.1, algebra]

claim:
## Definition

Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.

## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Keep a nonempty pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with $l=p_n>0$ columns of heights $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, the origin $c$, and $U_d=V_c^{\otimes d}$ of [[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. The **stable range** is $q_l\ge d$: there are at least $d$ rows of maximum length $l$. Put $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$, $A_d=\operatorname{im}(W(\lambda)\to\operatorname{End}U_d)$ and $B_d=\operatorname{im}(H_d(\mathbf a)\to\operatorname{End}U_d^{\mathrm{op}})$.

For every complex origin the finite image algebras are mutual centralizers, and the raw Hecke action is faithful in the stable range. For an **admissible** origin, meaning $c_j-c_k\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_j=c_k$, the following construction defines the central support outside that range. Append $t$ full ground rows of length $l$ until $q_l+t\ge d$, keeping $l$ and $c$ fixed. Then $n$ and every $q_j$ increase by $t$, so every $a_j$ stays fixed. In the enlarged tensor space $U_d^{\mathrm{big}}$, let $e$ be the projection onto tensors using only retained rows, equivalently having zero occupancy in every deleted row. A large tableau is **contractible** if every deleted-row entry is the ground entry $c_j+1-r$ in row $r$ and column $j$. The supporting central idempotent $f$ acts as one on precisely the contractible standard-labelled simples and as zero on the others. Through the faithful enlarged Hecke action it is a central idempotent of $H_d(\mathbf a)$, and
$$B_d\cong fH_d(\mathbf a)f,\qquad\ker\psi_d=(1-f)H_d(\mathbf a).$$

This $f$ is a sum of entire supporting central blocks. Individual residue idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$ need not be central; they do not individually define this two-sided corner. The unrestricted tensor model does not by itself supply the admissible central-support conclusion.

For the empty pyramid $l=N=0$, the convention is separate: in degree zero the tensor and image algebras are $\mathbb C$ with the identity corner $f=1$; in positive degree the tensor, image algebras and their module categories are zero and $f=0$. No $q_l$ or nonempty stable-range condition is used in that case.

Every term of the right tensor formula restricts identically under $v_{\mathbf i}\mapsto v_{\hat{\mathbf i}}$, because row and column positions and left neighbours agree and $c_j+(q_j+t)-(n+t)=a_j$. This proves the actual right-bimodule identification $eU^{\mathrm{big}}=U$ and a surjective restriction map $\rho:B_d^{\mathrm{big}}\to B_d$. The zero-occupancy part is $\mathbb C_{c_j}\otimes S_{\mu^{(j)}}(\mathbb C^{q_j})$, by the tensor Young-symmetrizer realization; it is zero precisely when a removed-row partition entry is nonzero. Every surviving path has only retained rows and is exactly a small path. ## Definition

Work over $\mathbb C$ and assume the Axiom of Choice where projective covers,
duality and locally unital assemblies enter. Let
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be admissible in the sense that
$c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$, and let
$\mathcal O_c^d$ be the relevant summand of the genuine parabolic
category $\mathcal O$ attached to the labels $c$ and the degree $d$: its
objects are the modules whose column-strict labels have nonnegative integral
differences from the ground entries of each column, i.e. the labels with
$\Lambda$-diagram content $c_j+q_j-n$ in the sense of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] (the ambient categories are the
ones of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
and [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]).

For a $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated object $N$ of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$, the **Whittaker functor** is the covariant finite-dimensional dual
$$V(N):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak m}(N,\mathbb C_\chi)^*.$$
Its $W(\lambda)$ action is obtained from the continuous $\chi$-part of the right
linear dual, then the reflected head/tail identification proved below. In the
notation $D_{\mathrm{row}}\mathrm{Wh}D_{\mathrm{row}}$, the middle Whittaker
operation is performed on this continuous $\chi$-part, not on the uncompleted
ordinary row-restricted dual. Write $N(A)$ for source standard objects,
$L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for source simples, and $L_W(A)$ for the resulting
nonzero simple $W$-modules. These namespaces are distinct.

The verification below records the properties used on this page: $V$ is exact
on the $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated objects of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$ and intertwines finite tensoring, the Casimir and the flips; $V$
is distinct from the Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$
constructed later; for the ground simple projective-injective $P_c$ and
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ one has $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and
$V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$; and $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))$ is the simple $W$-module $L_W(A)$ for
standard labels $A$ and zero otherwise. Nonintegral origins use the typed
equivalence of the all-weight Harish-Chandra comparison of the source; no
arbitrary complex $c$ is identified with an integral block. After fixing the
ground identification $i_0\colon V(P_c)\to\mathbb C_c$, the compatible functor
and the maps $j_d$ are unique up to the normalized unique natural isomorphism;
without this normalization scalar automorphisms prevent literal uniqueness.

(all boxes lie in one column, and the grading is concentrated in degree $0$):
$\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g^e=\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb C)$, $\mathfrak m=0$,
$\mathbb C_1[x_1,\dots,x_d]=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1,\dots,x_d)=\mathbb C$
and $\mathbb C_1[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]=\mathbb C[S_d]$. The stable range for
this $\lambda$ is $q_l\ge d$, i.e. $2\ge d$, so $d=1,2$ are exactly the stable
cases. The example verifies Vust's double centralizer
([[thm-vust-double-centralizer-for-the-type-a-nilpotent-centralizer]]) in these
cases.

claim:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. Let
$W_d=\varphi_d(W(\lambda))\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ be the
image of the finite W-algebra and let
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ be the image of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] under the right action. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$ and every $d$, and their associated graded image
   algebras are the corresponding images of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and of the
   truncated polynomial/permutation algebra.
2. For a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$, then the action of the full cyclotomic algebra
   $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful.
3. If $c$ is admissible (that is, $c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$),
   then the tensor module is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence
   between $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.

Mutual centralizers alone do not imply Morita for arbitrary $c$: the explicit
example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$, $d=2$ on the companion page has a
nonprojective tensor module.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. Let
$W_d=\varphi_d(W(\lambda))\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ be the
image of the finite W-algebra and let
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ be the image of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] under the right action. Then:

[F1] In the fixed loop chart, the associated graded left representation is the character-twisted Vust representation $X\mapsto\sum_tX^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}$. Its unital image is exactly the untwisted Vust image, because it is obtained by the automorphism $X\mapsto X+\kappa_c(X)1$ of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$. The right graded image is the ordinary truncated polynomial/permutation image. These image algebras are mutual centralizers for every Jordan type and every degree, including scalar degree zero and the empty-pyramid zero tensor case ([[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]], [[thm-vust-double-centralizer-for-the-type-a-nilpotent-centralizer]]).

[F2] $W(\lambda)$ has a separated loop filtration with associated graded $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, and the cyclotomic quotient has the bounded monomial basis $x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w$ with $0\le r_i<l$; both filtrations are compatible with the bimodule structure ([[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]], [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]).

[F3] The genuine original-head Whittaker comparison is exact, identifies induced standards with their head-normalized finite Levi modules and scalar content central characters, sends standard-labelled simples to the distinct exhaustive finite-image simples and other simples to zero, and intertwines both ordinary tensor functors with V and V* and the actual right Casimir/flip operators; the standard-label crystal supplies predecessor head quotients, and the category-O detector contains every standard projective cover and has only standard labels in its head and socle ([[thm-skryabins-equivalence-for-the-type-a-whittaker-pair]], [[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]]).
[F5] The genuine standard/Casimir interfaces proved in [[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]] supply the admissible character/quotient computations.

Context only: The stable injectivity criterion: if $e$ has at least $d$ strings of maximum length $l$, the longest-string vector realizes the regular right module, so the right action is injective ([[thm-vust-double-centralizer-for-the-type-a-nilpotent-centralizer]]).

1.1 The graded unital images. Write $E=V^{\otimes d}$, $C=W_d$, and $D$ for the right Hecke image viewed as an algebra of operators on $E$. The supplied actual tensor model in F1 gives commuting filtered operator algebras, with the graded symbols containing the unital images $A^0$ of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and $D^0$ of the truncated polynomial/permutation algebra. The character automorphism in F1 gives exactly the same $A^0$ as the untwisted representation; no equality of the fixed-chart twisted and untwisted modules is inferred. Since $A^0,D^0$ are mutual centralizers, taking leading homogeneous terms of commuting operators gives $A^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}C\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(D)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}D)\subseteq Z(D^0)=A^0$, where $Z$ is the commutant in $\operatorname{End}(E)$. Interchanging $C,D$ gives $D^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}D\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(C)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}C)\subseteq Z(A^0)=D^0$. Thus every inclusion is equality, establishing strict equality of both graded images as well as their commutants. [F1, F2, construct, algebra]

1.2 The exact ordinary-dual adjoint. For a finite rational $\mathfrak g$-module $E$, Skryabin transports ordinary evaluation $E^*\otimes E\to\mathbb C$ and coevaluation $\mathbb C\to E\otimes E^*$ to the tensor functors $F_E(M)=M\circledast E$. The ordinary zigzag identities give both adjunctions between $F_E$ and $F_{E^*}$. These functors are exact: tensoring is exact, it preserves generalized Whittaker modules by a finite Engel-flag nilpotence bound, and Skryabin is an exact equivalence. They preserve $\mathcal R_c$: a faithful finite image module embeds the regular algebra into a finite direct sum of copies of itself by evaluation on a basis, so every finite-image module is a subquotient of a finite sum of tensor modules; exact tensor transport sends degree $d$ to degree $d+1$. For $N>0$, also $V^*=\bigwedge^{N-1}V\otimes\det^{-1}$, and the exterior power is a summand of a tensor power by the antisymmetrizer. Determinant shifts therefore give closure under $V^*$ too. Consequently $F_V$ preserves projectives in the entire rational category through its exact right adjoint $F_{V^*}$. Here $V^*$ is the ordinary contragredient natural module, distinct from $V$; the transpose contravariant duality of category $\mathcal O$ is not this adjoint. [F3, construct, algebra]

2.1 The filtered centralizers. For an operator in $Z(D)$, equality of the induced graded spaces in step 1.1 supplies a member of $C$ with the same leading symbol. Subtracting lowers its integer filtration degree. The finite grading of $E$ bounds the induced endomorphism filtration below, so this terminates, proving $Z(D)=C$. The same procedure proves $Z(C)=D$. Returning to the right-action opposite convention gives both mutual-centralizer identities and the stated associated graded image algebras. At degree zero both images are scalar, while for an empty pyramid and positive degree $E=0$ and both are zero; these are already covered by the actual tensor model of F1. This proves clause (1) for every origin, without a Morita assumption. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Stable injectivity. For a nonempty pyramid with $q_l\ge d$, choose $d$ distinct terminal boxes on length-$l$ Jordan strings. In the associated graded tensor action each bounded PBW word $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_d^{a_d}w$, $0\le a_i<l$, sends their ordered terminal tensor to the tensor with those distinct strings permuted by $w$ and each box moved $a_i$ places left. These $l^dd!$ outputs are distinct basis tensors, so the graded PBW word images are independent. A nonzero filtered Hecke element has a nonzero leading PBW symbol, hence a nonzero leading operator and a nonzero actual operator. Thus the raw action is faithful. For the empty pyramid, degree zero is the scalar identity and positive-degree tensor space and cyclotomic algebra are zero, so the action is faithful there too without using an undefined $q_l$. [F1, F2, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

Its content reconstructs it uniquely among column-strict tableaux: in each charge coset the minimum appears in every column and hence in its bottom box; removing these boxes and repeating reconstructs all columns. Therefore its scalar central-character summand has exactly this one simple, by F3. The regular-module multiplicity of $D_r$ is one. Indeed, the Levi decomposition of $Z_\nu$ uses semistandard tableaux of shapes given by the column partitions of ground differences, with the alphabet in column $j$ consisting of the terminal row boxes whose rows reach that column. This follows by expanding the complete symmetric characters of its symmetric factors and using the Schur semistandard formula, or successive horizontal-strip multiplication; its finite radical filtration makes it an actual $\mathfrak p$-filtration by these Levi sections. For $D_r$ the shapes are rectangles $(r^{q_j})$ and the allowed alphabet has exactly $q_j$ letters. Each length-$q_j$ strictly increasing tableau column must contain every letter in order. There is exactly one tuple, and its row-$i$ multiplicity is $rp_i$. Thus the coefficient is one for $\nu_i=rp_i$ and zero for every other occupancy. Other standards cannot contain $D_r$ because their scalar central characters differ. The supported regular summand has length one and is $D_r$ itself, so $D_r$ is projective over $W_{Nr}$. For a surjection in the rational finite-W category $\mathcal R_c$, a common determinant twist puts its terms into finite sums of polynomial-image categories. The scalar degree operator splits these by degree. A map from $\mathbb C_c$ becomes a map from $D_r$ into the degree-$Nr$ summand, where it lifts by the projectivity just proved. The inverse determinant twist gives the original lift. Hence $\mathbb C_c$ is projective in $\mathcal R_c$, without claiming projectivity in arbitrary $W(\lambda)$-mod. For a positive-degree standard $A$, the actual standard-label crystal supplies $A=\widetilde f_iB$ and a quotient $L_O(B)\otimes V\to L_O(A)$. Lifting along the projective cover and splitting proves $P(A)$ is a summand of $P(B)\otimes V$. The genuine tensor comparison sends this to a summand of $Q(B)\circledast V$, projective by step 1.2. To identify its head, write $P(B)\otimes V=\bigoplus_C P(C)^{m_C}$ with standard $C$, using the independently proved detector head/socle property in F3. Exact Wh gives $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_W(Q(C),L_W(D))\ge\delta_{CD}$. This uses the actual simple-image and tensor maps of F3, rather than inferring covers from characters or mutual centralizers. [F3, step 4.1, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

claim:
## Statement refuted

**Refuted claim:** the characteristic-zero generic comparison between the
integrally charged degenerate tower and the nondegenerate tower can be
specialized to every nonzero Hecke parameter, thereby transporting the
degenerate Ariki theorem to every nondegenerate parameter without further
comparison results.

Already over $\mathbb C$, at level one, charge $m\in\mathbb Z$ and rank two,
the full degenerate algebra is $\mathbb C[S_2]$, whereas the nondegenerate
algebra at $\xi=-1$ is $\mathbb C[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$. They have two
and one simple modules, respectively, and are not isomorphic. Thus the
claimed universal algebra transport is false. This refutes the proposed
method of inference; it does not assert that the nondegenerate Ariki theorem
itself is false or cannot be proved using additional results.

The genuine generic comparison and generic categorification equivalence
remain in their characteristic-zero, infinite-order, integral-charge scope,
as recorded in
[[rem-degenerate-and-nondegenerate-ariki-theorems-have-distinct-parameter-ranges]].
The full generic based/tower branch remains dependent on the coherent
comparison and standard-class dictionary, rather than on unrelated
rankwise algebra isomorphisms alone.

[F2] The defining relations of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] at rank two are
$s^2=1$, $x_1x_2=x_2x_1$, $sx_2=x_1s+1$ and $x_2s=sx_1+1$.

1.1 In the degenerate quotient $x_1=m$ and $sx_2=ms+1$ give $x_2=m+s$. Hence the quotient is generated by $s$ with $s^2=1$. Their bounded PBW words are a subset of the bounded basis of $A$, so the generator-preserving homomorphism is injective. Let $w_t=s_t\cdots s_d$ for $1\le t\le d$ and $w_{d+1}=1$; these are the minimal right $S_d$ coset representatives in $S_{d+1}$, with $w_t(d+1)=t$. In the associated graded algebra their symbols are the distinct bounded words obtained by permuting the first $d$ dot exponents by $w_t$ and placing exponent $r$ in the omitted position $t$, with permutation $w_tv$, $v\in S_d$. 2.1 **An actual relative Frobenius trace.** Use the two symmetric traces to define $t:A\to B$ uniquely by $\tau_d(bt(a))=\tau_{d+1}(ba)$ for every $b\in B$. Nondegeneracy of $\tau_d$ proves existence and uniqueness. Cyclicity of both traces gives $t(b_1ab_2)=b_1t(a)b_2$, so $t$ is a $B$-bimodule map. The map $\Phi:A\to\operatorname{Hom}_B({}_BA,{}_BB)$, $\Phi(a)(c)=t(ca)$, is an $(A,B)$-bimodule isomorphism, where the left action on Hom is $(a\cdot h)(c)=h(ca)$ and its right action is multiplication on the output. Cross relations show $x_{d+1}$ commutes with $B$, so $u_i$ centralizes $B$ and is fixed by $*$. Their products and sum give the stated orthogonality and identity. ## Example

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the categorification and based-module identifications; the explicit finite calculations below are choice-free.

For $I=\{0\}$ and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$, the degree-one supported block
$B=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ ([[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]])
has simple $D_{01}=\mathbb C$ with $x\mapsto0$ and projective cover $Y_{01}=B$.
Therefore $[Y_{01}]=2[D_{01}]$ in $G_0$, whereas
$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{01},D_{01})=1$. At parameter one the categorification
images of [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]] and
[[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]]
are

$$P_{00}=D_{00}=M_{00},\qquad P_{01}=M_{01}+M_{10},\qquad D_{01}=\tfrac12(M_{01}+M_{10}),\qquad P_{11}=D_{11}=M_{11}.$$

The simple image is the PROJECTED vector $\pi L_{01}$, not the unprojected
$L_{01}=M_{01}$. With the normalized highest pairing $C_0$ one has
$C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ across these three weights. In the degree-two block
$M_2(\mathbb C)$, the simple $D_{11}$ is two-dimensional and is itself its
projective cover; the abstract Fock weight is one-dimensional, not the
underlying module. Thus the composition Cartan values are $1,2,1$, while the
projective/simple Hom pairing is the identity. Projective covers are self-dual
here by the actual symmetric block forms, not merely because their heads are
self-dual.

In the costandard basis $(D_{00},D_{01},D_{11})$,

$$fD_{00}=2D_{01},\quad fD_{01}=D_{11},\quad fD_{11}=0;\qquad eD_{00}=0,\quad eD_{01}=D_{00},\quad eD_{11}=2D_{01}.$$

The divided powers give $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$ and $e^{(2)}D_{11}=D_{00}$, with
all other second divided moves $0$. Hence the integral ground-generated lattice
is EXACTLY $\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus2\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$, of index
$2$ in the full costandard lattice
$\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$. The standard lattice
has basis $(P_{00},P_{01},P_{11})$, is integrally divided-power generated by its
ground, and pairs perfectly with the full costandard lattice. Costandard ground
cyclicity holds over $\mathbb Q$, not over $\mathbb Z$; crystal and
composition-factor reachability do not imply integral vector generation.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an admissible origin $c$; let
$f_i^{\mathcal O},e_i^{\mathcal O}$ be the residue translation functors on the
sum of parabolic blocks of
[[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]] and let
$f_i^{H},e_i^{H}$ be the Hecke residue functors of
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]].
Then there are natural isomorphisms
$$f_i^{H}\pi\cong\pi f_i^{\mathcal O},\qquad e_i^{H}\pi\cong\pi e_i^{\mathcal O},$$
where $\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ is the Schur functor of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]],
compatible with the residue eigenvalue projectors, the units and counits of the
evaluation/coevaluation adjunction and its dual transported reverse adjunction, and with ordinary restricted duality and the $*$-duality of the
Hecke side. Consequently the ungraded Grothendieck operators at parameter $1$
agree and the Schur quotient induces a homomorphism for the enveloping-algebra Chevalley action. For
admissible nonintegral origins the category $\mathcal O$ side uses the genuine
typed coset realization, not an unqualified integer block. The statement
preserves the actual residue and standard filtrations; no graded parity or
Koszul lift is asserted by these ungraded suppliers.

[F2] The Hecke-side residue functors are exact, biadjoint, commute with the $*$-duality, and their operators are adjoint for the Cartan pairing ([[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]]).

[F3] The Schur functor is exact, kills exactly the off-standard simples and sends standards to intrinsic Specht modules. Its tensor detector $T_d$ is prinjective, its Hecke endomorphism algebra is $B_d$, and its Whittaker image $U_d$ is a projective generator of the corresponding finite-W image category. There are natural identifications $\gamma_M:\pi_dM\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U_d,\mathrm{Wh}M)$ and the coherent tensor isomorphisms $\nu_M:\mathrm{Wh}(M\otimes V)\cong\mathrm{Wh}(M)\circledast V$, with $\mu_d:U_d\circledast V\cong U_{d+1}$ intertwining the tower generators. In the stable realization $B_d$ is the full cyclotomic algebra, while content projections give the supported blocks. Every category-O projective has a copresentation $0\to P\to T_1\to T_2$ with $T_1,T_2\in\operatorname{add}(T_d)$. These are the actual Whittaker/Morita, copresentation and tensor contracts of [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]], [[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]], [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-endomorphism-isomorphism]] and [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]].

1.1 **Restriction uses the dual natural module.** For $N$ in the degree-$(d+1)$ summand and a basis $v_a$ of $V$ with dual basis $v^a$, tensor adjunction gives the natural map $\rho_N:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_{d+1},N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_d,N\otimes V^*)$, $\rho_N(h)(t)=\sum_a h(t\otimes v_a)\otimes v^a$. Its inverse sends $g$ to $(t\otimes v)\mapsto(1\otimes\operatorname{ev}_v)g(t)$. These maps are basis-independent by coevaluation and evaluation and commute with the first $d$ tower generators, acting on the $T_d$ factors. Thus they identify restriction of $\pi_{d+1}N$ with $\pi_d(N\otimes V^*)$ after the appropriate degree/block projection. The natural and dual natural modules are distinct $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-modules; no identification between them is used. [F1, F3, construct, algebra]

1.2 **The induction map is an actual tensor map.** For $M$ of degree $d$, put $\tau_M:B_{d+1}\otimes_{B_d}\pi_dM\to\pi_{d+1}(M\otimes V)$, $b\otimes f\mapsto(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)\circ R_b$, where $R_b$ is the right action on $T_{d+1}$. The first $d$ generators act on $T_d$, so this expression is balanced over $B_d$ and is $B_{d+1}$-linear for the left-module convention; naturality follows by postcomposition. To prove it invertible, on the finite-W side form $\sigma_X(b\otimes g)=(g\circledast\mathrm{id}_V)\circ\mu_d^{-1}\circ R_b$. For $X=U_d$ this is the regular-module isomorphism $B_{d+1}\otimes_{B_d}B_d\cong B_{d+1}$. It remains an isomorphism on finite sums and summands. Every finite-W image object has a finite projective presentation by summands of finite sums of $U_d$, and both sides are right exact: induction is right exact, tensoring with $V$ is exact and Hom from $U_d,U_{d+1}$ is exact. Passing to cokernels proves $\sigma_X$ invertible for all $X$. The coherent $\gamma,\nu,\mu$ square of [F3] sends $1\otimes f$ by either route to $(\mathrm{Wh}(f)\circledast\mathrm{id}_V)\mu_d^{-1}$; $B_{d+1}$-linearity then makes the square commute on every $b\otimes f$. Consequently $\tau_M$ is invertible for every $M$. This presentation argument takes place in the finite-W image category, where $U_d$ is a full projective generator; it does not assert that $T_d$ is a full category-O generator. [F3, construct, algebra]

2.1 **The two residue projectors.** The tower's last dot on $T_d\otimes V$ is the tensor Casimir, with the normalization of [F1]. Hence $\tau$ intertwines its generalized-$i$ eigenprojector with the projector defining $f_i^{\mathcal O}$. On the dual tensor factor one has the actual operator identity $\Omega_{N,V^*}\rho_N(h)=-\rho_N(h\Omega_{T_d,V})-n\rho_N(h)$. Indeed $E_{ba}v^c=-\delta_{bc}v^a$ and equivariance of $h$ give the first term $-\sum_{a,b}h(E_{ab}t\otimes v_b)\otimes v^a$ and the second term $-n\sum_a h(t\otimes v_a)\otimes v^a$, exactly that identity. Thus the last-dot generalized-$i$ projector corresponds to the dual-Casimir generalized-$(-n-i)$ projector, including its nilpotent part. This is the actual adjunction mate and agrees with the flag normalization in [F1]. Under $\rho$ the last-dot projector therefore corresponds to the generalized-$(-n-i)$ projector defining $e_i^{\mathcal O}$. Applying the source content projector $e_\alpha$ and target projector $e_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ to steps 1.1–1.2 gives $u_{\alpha,i}\pi_{\alpha+\alpha_i}N\cong\pi_\alpha e_i^{\mathcal O}N$ and $B_{\alpha+\alpha_i}u_{\alpha,i}\otimes_{B_\alpha}\pi_\alpha M\cong\pi_{\alpha+\alpha_i}f_i^{\mathcal O}M$. Polynomial generalized-eigenspace projectors commute with these natural maps because the maps intertwine the operators, proving the asserted residue compatibility. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 **The natural duality comparison.** The ordinary category-O duality $D$ uses matrix transpose and restricted weight-space duals. The product of the ground contravariant form and the natural-factor forms gives a nondegenerate detector form $(xtb,t')=(t,x^{\mathrm{tr}}t'b^*)$; the Casimir, crossings and content projectors are self-adjoint. Put $\delta M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,T_d)$ with $(bf)(m)=f(m)b^*$ and $X^\#=\operatorname{Hom}_{B_d}(X,B_d)$ with the same twist. The detector form gives an actual isomorphism $\beta:T_d\cong DT_d$, $\beta(t)(t')=(t,t')$. Exact restricted contravariant duality, with its canonical bidual map, consequently gives $\delta M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,T_d)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,DT_d)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_d,DM)=\pi_dDM$. Its explicit map is $f\mapsto[t\mapsto(m\mapsto(t,f(m)))]$; its inverse sends $g:T_d\to DM$ to $\beta^{-1}\circ Dg\circ\operatorname{bidual}_M:M\to T_d$. These maps are inverse by the symmetry and nondegeneracy of the form and the bidual identities, and the form's $*$-invariance makes them Hecke-linear. This is a canonical natural Hom-duality isomorphism; it requires neither dimensions of simple images nor self-duality of individual projective summands. Tensor-Hom gives $\delta\pi_d^*\cong\#$, while the symmetric trace of [F2] gives $\#\cong D_H$ by $h\mapsto\mathrm{tr}\circ h$. Define $\theta_M:M\to D\pi_d^*\delta M$ by $\theta_M(m)(t\otimes f)=(t,f(m))$. The displayed form identity makes it balanced over $B_d$ and $\mathfrak g$-linear. Applying $\pi_d$ gives a natural transformation $\pi_d\to\pi_dD\pi_d^*\delta\cong\#\pi_dD$ between exact functors. It is an isomorphism on $T_d$ and hence on its finite sums and summands. Apply the copresentations in [F3] to prove it an isomorphism on every projective, by exactness and kernels; then apply projective presentations to prove it on every object, by cokernels. Dualizing yields the natural comparison $\pi_dD\cong D_H\pi_d$. The product forms, tensor evaluation and trace form are the same forms used for the dual adjunctions; consequently this comparison identifies their dual unit/counit squares. Since the residue projectors are self-adjoint, it also commutes with each $f_i,e_i$ separately. Thus $Df_i\cong f_iD$ and $De_i\cong e_iD$. None of this identifies the usual tensor dual $V^*$ with $V$. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

3.2 **Grothendieck operators and quotient.** Exactness of $\pi$ and of the residue functors makes the natural isomorphisms of step 2.1 induce $[f_i^H][\pi]=[\pi][f_i^{\mathcal O}]$ and $[e_i^H][\pi]=[\pi][e_i^{\mathcal O}]$. On $G_0$, the source simple-class basis shows that $\ker[\pi]$ is exactly the span of the off-standard simple classes, and the induced map from this quotient onto $G_0(H)$ is an isomorphism. No isomorphism from the entire category-O Grothendieck group is asserted. On split projective groups only $\operatorname{add}(T)$ is equivalent to Hecke projectives; an ambient off-standard projective need not have projective image. These distinctions leave the displayed operator equalities intact. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **Adjunction maps.** The first tensor unit is the coevaluation $m\mapsto\sum_a(m\otimes v_a)\otimes v^a$, and the tensor counit is evaluation. The induction/restriction unit is $z\mapsto1\otimes z$, and the counit is $b\otimes z\mapsto bz$. Substituting these formulas into $\tau$ and $\rho$ gives the same composite maps, term by term: coevaluation is precisely the sum in $\rho$, and evaluation cancels that sum by $v^a(v_b)=\delta_{ab}$. Restricting the commuting squares by the content and residue projectors proves compatibility for $f_i\dashv e_i$. For the reverse adjunction use the biadjoint mate maps supplied by [F1] and the symmetric-trace reverse adjunction of [F2]; transport the latter through $\tau,\rho$. The transported evaluation and coevaluation pair is the O-side biadjoint pair, since its dot and crossing mates agree with those in [F1], with the same trace normalization. Equivalently the reverse unit and counit are the dual mates of the first pair, so the same squares commute. The two pairs are thus compared with their transported normalizations; this is stronger than asserting abstract uniqueness of adjoints across a quotient. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 **Filtrations and boundaries.** Applying exact $\pi$ to the O-side residue standard flags preserves their successive quotients, and the intertwined generalized-eigenvalue projectors select the corresponding residue pieces. Admissible nonintegral origins retain the typed coset realization of [F4]; an integral highest-weight Fock interpretation is used only on its actual integral residue component. All comparisons here are ungraded at parameter one. Together with steps 2.1–3.2 this proves the statement. [F1, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 4.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, given] ∎

## Statement

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the category-O, Fock/global and Schur quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below charge hypothesis: $I$ is a nonempty set of consecutive
integers bounded below and $\Lambda\in P^+$ has level $l$ and integral
multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ in the letter alphabet $I^+$. Use the actual admissible integral-origin stable realization of the tower definition, with roots $c_j+q_j-n_{\rm row}=m_j$. Then the two identifications of the preceding
theorems hold simultaneously for the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower
$H^\Lambda$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]:
$K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ and
$G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$, and they are mutually dual under the
Cartan and Shapovalov pairings. Moreover:

**(i)** for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ one has
$[S(B)]=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)[D(A)]$, where
$d_{A,B}(s)\in\mathbb Z[s]$ is defined by $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$
(equivalently $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$);

**(ii)** the endomorphisms of both Grothendieck groups induced by $e_i,f_i$
$(i\in I)$ are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ of
$\dot U_{\mathbb Z}(\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+})$;

**(iii)** for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $i\in I$ the module $e_iD(A)$
(resp. $f_iD(A)$) is nonzero if and only if $\tilde e_i(A)\ne\varnothing$
(resp. $\tilde f_i(A)\ne\varnothing$), in which case it is a self-dual
indecomposable module with irreducible socle and head isomorphic to
$D(\tilde e_i(A))$ (resp. $D(\tilde f_i(A))$);

**(iv)** in the source's normalization the projective classes correspond to the
quasi-canonical family $P_A$, which at parameter one equals the canonical
family on $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ ($P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ at $s=1$), while the
simple classes correspond to the dual-canonical family
$D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$, the label bijections being $\uparrow:\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha$ and its inverse rectification $\downarrow:\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For any admitted consecutive $I$, including $\mathbb Z$ and half-infinite sets,
the same blockwise statements hold: for a fixed $\alpha$ and finite list of
residue operations choose lower and upper cuts whose LETTER alphabet contains
every charge and whose ROOT interval contains the support of $\alpha$ and the
required shifted supports; added bottom tails are common ground and added top
entries are absent, and the double-cut compatibility and the
contractible-central-corner restriction identify these SAME Hecke blocks,
intrinsic Spechts, projective/simple labels and residue maps. These compatible
finite pieces give the original arbitrary-$I$ statement. At level $0$ only
$\alpha=0$ and the ground survive.

Assume the bounded-below charge hypothesis: $I$ is a nonempty set of consecutive
integers bounded below and $\Lambda\in P^+$ has level $l$ and integral
multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ in the letter alphabet $I^+$. Use the actual admissible integral-origin stable realization of the tower definition, with roots $c_j+q_j-n_{\rm row}=m_j$. Then the two identifications of the preceding
theorems hold simultaneously for the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower
$H^\Lambda$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]:
$K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ and
$G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$, and they are mutually dual under the
Cartan and Shapovalov pairings. Moreover:

**Given:** The bounded-below data and the tower $H^\Lambda$ of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], the two
identifications of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
and [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]],
the Fock data of [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] with its four
families of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and
the category-O side of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
as well as the Axiom of Choice as used by the imported suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). We prove (i)-(iv) and the arbitrary-$I$ extension.

1.1 **Both identifications and their duality.** By [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] the map $[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$ identifies $G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ with the full integral costandard lattice $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ and is compatible with the standard classes $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$; by [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]] the map $[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ identifies $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))$ with the standard lattice $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$, the embedding of projectives induces the lattice inclusion, and the Cartan pairing is the normalized highest pairing $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ of [[lem-the-fock-pairing-matches-projective-simple-and-standard-costandard-pairings]]. Since the two lattice identifications are the actual source dictionary $[L(A)]\mapsto L_A$, $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$ of [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]] at parameter one, the identifications hold simultaneously and are mutually dual. [F2, given, algebra]

1.2 **The actual surviving-head calculation.** Fix $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and let $M=f_i^{\mathcal O}L(A)$, or $M=e_i^{\mathcal O}L(A)$. The local residue theorem [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]] says $M=0$ exactly when the corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise its head is the simple $L(C)$ at that edge, and it is self-dual. The ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ is closed under the two crystal operators by [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], so $C$ is standard. The actual detector/corner Hom comparison of [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]] applies to maps from a Std-head object to a Std-socle object. Applying it to $M$ and $L(B)$ for each standard $B$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_H(\pi M,D(B))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,L(B))$, of dimension $\delta_{CB}$. Since the $D(B)$ are the complete distinct Hecke simples, this computes the head of $\pi M$ as the single simple $D(C)$ and proves $\pi M\ne0$. The natural intertwining of [[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]] identifies $\pi M$ with the appropriate Hecke translate of $D(A)$, and its natural duality comparison makes that translate self-dual. Its socle is therefore also $D(C)$. A direct sum of two nonzero finite-length modules has at least two nonzero simple head summands, so a module with simple head is indecomposable. 1.4 **Level zero.** For level $0$ the tower has $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$ and $H^\Lambda_d=0$ for $d>0$ by the level-zero convention of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], so only $\alpha=0$ and the ground class remain, consistently with the two identifications being the rank-one lattices $\mathbb ZP_\varnothing=\mathbb ZD_\varnothing$. 2.2 **The Chevalley operators (ii).** The residue operators on $G_0$ are the Chevalley operators by [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]], and the corresponding statement on $K_0$ for projective classes is [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]]; on the category-O side both statements are the integrable Fock action of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]] transferred by the actual natural residue comparisons. This proves (ii). [step 1.1, step 1.2, given, algebra]

2.3 **Arbitrary consecutive $I$.** Let $I$ be any nonempty consecutive set (possibly unbounded above or below), fix a content $\alpha$ and a finite list of residue operations, and choose a finite lower endpoint $k$ and upper endpoint $r$ so that the LETTER alphabet $[k,r+1]$ contains every charge and the ROOT interval $[k,r]$ contains the support of $\alpha$ and every shifted support occurring in the operations. ## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c$, a degree $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space with its finite W-algebra image
$W_d$ and cyclotomic Hecke image $B_d$. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$; this is the raw double centralizer.
2. For admissible origins, $V_c^{\otimes d}$ is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence between
   $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.
3. The genuine Whittaker functor followed by this equivalence is the exact
   Schur Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples; it is fully
   faithful on all projectives of the relevant parabolic summand and on all
   tiltings, and its left adjoint is right exact and recovers
   $\operatorname{add}(T)$ but need not recover every projective.
4. For a nonempty pyramid, in the stable range $q_l\ge d$ the algebra $B_d$ is the full cyclotomic
   algebra $H_d(\mathbf a)$; outside the stable range and for admissible
   origins the central-corner identification $B_d=fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ is used.

Mutual centralizers alone do not give the Morita statement: the nonadmissible
origin example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$ and $d=2$ has a nonprojective tensor
module while the mutual centralizer identities still hold.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c$ be an admissible origin, let $P_c$ be the ground
simple projective-injective of the relevant summand of the parabolic category
$\mathcal O$ of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
and let $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ with $V=\mathbb C^N$. Write
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ for the image of the right cyclotomic Hecke action of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] and $B_\alpha$ for its central
components. Then the right Hecke action gives an algebra isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d,$$
and on each central component, cut by the central idempotents $f_\alpha$ of
$B_d$ acting on $T=\bigoplus_\alpha T_\alpha$,
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_\alpha =f_\alpha H_\alpha(\mathbf a)f_\alpha,$$
where $H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$ is the corresponding block of the cyclotomic Hecke
algebra. For a nonempty pyramid, in the stable range $q_l\ge d$ the image is the full cyclotomic
algebra, $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ and $B_\alpha=H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$; a single
component is not identified with the entire degree-$d$ algebra. Outside the
stable range the central-corner identification uses the admissible-origin
corner of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The maps $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ are surjective in all cases,
and the full action $H_d(\mathbf a)\to\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ is
injective precisely when $q_l\ge d$ for a nonempty pyramid. For the empty pyramid $l=N=0$, the degree-zero objects and algebras are $T_0=U_0=H_0=\mathbb C$, and for $d>0$ they are $T_d=U_d=H_d=0$. All endomorphism identities hold there, and the raw action is faithful in every degree, including the zero-algebra action; $q_l$ is not defined in this branch.

[F1] The right Hecke action on $T$ exists and its generators $x_j,s_i$ are natural endomorphisms of the tensor functor, commuting with $\mathfrak g$; the image is $B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$, and the Whittaker functor sends $T$ to $V_c^{\otimes d}$ ([[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]], [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]], [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]]).

[F2] The Whittaker functor is exact on $\mathcal O_c^d$, its kernel is the Serre subcategory generated by the off-standard simples, $T$ is a self-dual prinjective detector whose simple socle constituents are standard-labelled and whose indecomposable summands are precisely the standard-labelled projective-injective covers, each occurring with positive multiplicity, and $V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$ ([[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]], [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]]).

[F3] The filtered double centralizer identifies the two image algebras on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ for every complex origin: $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers, and in particular $\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d$; for a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$ the full action of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful ([[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]]).

[F4] Outside the stable range the image of the Hecke action is a central block corner $fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ for admissible origins, and in the stable range $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ ([[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]).

- The opposite algebra convention in $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the one fixed in [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]]: the right Hecke action composed left-to-right matches the left action of $B_\alpha$ on the modules of the Schur functor.

1.1 The Hecke action lies in the g-endomorphisms. For the empty pyramid, the empty tensor in degree zero and its ground object give $T_0=U_0=H_0=\mathbb C$. In positive degree $V=0$ gives $T_d=U_d=0$, and the level-zero cyclotomic relation is the empty product $1$, so $H_d=0$. The stated endomorphism identities and faithfulness follow directly, with the unique zero-algebra map injective; the remaining argument assumes a nonempty pyramid. Each generator $x_j$ of the truncated tensor action is built from the trace Casimir and place permutations and commutes with the diagonal $\mathfrak g$-action; the place permutations are natural in the module variable, so the resulting right $H_d(\mathbf a)$-action on $T$ consists of $\mathfrak g$-endomorphisms, and its image is $B_d$ by definition. Hence there is a surjection $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ and an inclusion $B_d\subseteq\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with the opposite convention fixed by the right action. [F1, algebra]

1.2 The Whittaker comparison is injective. Let $\varphi:T\to T$ be nonzero and put $X=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, a nonzero submodule of the finite-length object $T$. Choose a simple submodule $L(A)\subseteq X$; because $\operatorname{soc}X\subseteq\operatorname{soc}T$, [F2] gives $A\in\mathrm{Std}$. Exactness gives an injection $V(L(A))\hookrightarrow V(X)$, and the first module is nonzero, so $V(X)\ne0$. Exactness also identifies $V(X)$ with the image of $V(\varphi)$, hence $V(\varphi)\ne0$. This proves injectivity of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$. No restriction on all composition factors of $T$ is used. [F2, algebra]

2.1 The image of the comparison. On $V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$ the induced map lands in the centralizer of the finite-W action, $\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$; by the filtered double centralizer [F3] this centralizer equals $B_d$; and the induced map contains $B_d$ because every Hecke generator on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ arises from the corresponding endomorphism of $T$ by [F1]. Since $B_d$ is the whole target, the injective map of step 1.2 is also surjective, so $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d$. [F1, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 Stable range. For a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$ then the action of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful by [F3] and the image is the full algebra $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$; a single central component is correspondingly a block $H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$, not the whole algebra. Outside the stable range the corner identification of [F4] applies for admissible origins, while the map $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ remains surjective by step 1.1. [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Central components. The central idempotents $f_\alpha$ of the finite-dimensional algebra $B_d$ decompose $T=\bigoplus_\alpha T_\alpha$ and $B_d=\bigoplus_\alpha B_\alpha$; applying the isomorphism of step 2.1 componentwise gives $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}=f_\alpha B_df_\alpha=B_\alpha$. The component $B_\alpha$ sits inside the cyclotomic block as the corner $f_\alpha H_\alpha(\mathbf a)f_\alpha$ by [F4]; it is not the entire degree-$d$ algebra. [F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Failure of raw faithfulness below the stable range. For a nonempty pyramid, suppose $d>q_l$ and use an enlargement by full ground rows with smallest height at least $d$. In its last column, raise the first $q_l+1$ entries above their ground values by $1$; raise its top entry further by $d-q_l-1$, and leave every other entry ground. This is column strict, has total degree $d$, and is standard: for columns with the same charge, the changed rightmost entry is at least every unchanged entry to its left in that row; different charge cosets are incomparable. The first $q_l$ rows of this column are retained, but its next row is deleted, so this standard label is noncontractible. Its nonzero large finite-W simple belongs to a complementary central block. Hence the supporting idempotent $f$ of [F4] is proper; the faithful large tensor progenerator makes $1-f$ nonzero also in the large Hecke algebra. The small raw action has the nonzero kernel $(1-f)H_d(\mathbf a)$ and is not faithful. Together with step 2.2 this proves the asserted precise stable-range criterion. [F2, F4, step 2.2, construct, algebra] ∎

claim:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an admissible origin $c$. Let
$\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ be the Schur functor of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]],
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Use the current category-O namespace:
$N(A):=M(A)$ is the generalized standard, $K(A):=\nabla(A)$ the costandard,
$L(A)$ the category-O simple and $P(A)$ its projective cover, as in
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The source17 symbol $K(A)$ denotes our $L(A)$, not our costandard $K(A)$.
Write $\mathsf L(A):=\mathrm{Wh}(L(A))$ for the finite-W image of the
category-O simple; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ this is the source finite-W simple
appearing in the Whittaker/Morita contract of
[[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]].
In particular the $W_d$-Hom below takes a finite-W module as its second
argument. Let $\mathrm{Std}$ be the standard labels. Then:

1. For every label $A$, the Schur image of the standard object $N(A)$ is the
   intrinsic affine-induced Specht module
   $$S(A)=H_d\otimes_{H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}}\Bigl(\bigotimes_j \mathrm{ev}^*_{a_j}S^{\mu^{(j)}}\Bigr),\qquad a_j=c_j+q_j-n,$$
   where $\mu^{(j)}$ is the partition of $d_j$ read from the nonnegative
   ground differences in the $j$-th column of $A$ and the factors are induced
   along the affine Young subalgebra $H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}=H_{d_1}\otimes\cdots
   \otimes H_{d_l}$. Its affine action factors through the cyclotomic image $B_d$, so the same module is obtained by replacing $H_d$ in this tensor product by $H_d(\mathbf a)$.
2. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ the module
   $D(A)=\pi(L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))$ is
   simple, the modules $D(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, form a complete set of
   pairwise non-isomorphic simples of the Hecke image $B_d$, and
   $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$.
3. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, $\pi(P(A))$ is the projective cover $Y(A)$ of
   $D(A)$, and $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$; ambient off-standard projectives
   still have their genuine images, and no projective-preservation assertion
   is made for them.
4. Images of tiltings carry the opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag
   coefficients, and $\pi$ is fully faithful on tiltings.
5. For $A\in\mathrm{Col}$ and $B\in\mathrm{Std}$,
   $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$, where $d_{B,A}$ is the typed
   canonical-basis coefficient of the Fock-space dictionary; for $B\notin
   \mathrm{Std}$ the symbol $D(B)$ is not a Hecke simple. All interfaces are
   ungraded at parameter $1$.
