Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an admissible origin $c$. Let
$\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ be the Schur functor of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]],
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Use the current category-O namespace:
$N(A):=M(A)$ is the generalized standard, $K(A):=\nabla(A)$ the costandard,
$L(A)$ the category-O simple and $P(A)$ its projective cover, as in
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The source17 symbol $K(A)$ denotes our $L(A)$, not our costandard $K(A)$.
Write $\mathsf L(A):=\mathrm{Wh}(L(A))$ for the finite-W image of the
category-O simple; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ this is the source finite-W simple
appearing in the Whittaker/Morita contract of
[[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]].
In particular the $W_d$-Hom below takes a finite-W module as its second
argument. Let $\mathrm{Std}$ be the standard labels. Then:

[F2] The Schur functor $\pi$ is exact, kills exactly the off-standard simples, recovers $\operatorname{add}(T)$ under $\pi^*\pi$, and is fully faithful on all projectives and on all tiltings; $T$ contains every standard-labelled projective-injective cover ([[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]], [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]]).

[F3] The filtered double centralizer identifies $B_d=\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the Schur quotient is the composite of the genuine Whittaker functor with the Morita equivalence; the stable range gives $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ ([[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]], [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-endomorphism-isomorphism]], [[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]], [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]).

[F5] The cyclotomic Hecke algebra has the bounded monomial basis and the affine evaluation homomorphisms $\mathrm{ev}_{a}\colon H_{d_j}\to\mathbb C[S_{d_j}]$, $x_k\mapsto a+\sum_{h<k}(h,k)$ ([[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]).

1.1 **A regular corner in the stable realization.** Add full ground rows until there are $d$ distinct rows of length $l$, and choose one rightmost box in each such row; let $v_S$ be their ordered tensor and $e_S$ the row-weight projection onto tensors using these rows once each. The actual tensor matrices in [F3] preserve row multisets, so this projection commutes with the right Hecke action and belongs to the left image by the first centralizer. The vectors $v_Sx_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w$, $0\le r_i<l$, $w\in S_d$, have distinct leading tensors: the leading dot moves its box one column left, while a permutation changes the ordered distinct rows. They therefore form a basis of $e_SU$ by triangularity, and its cardinality is $l^dd!$. Thus $b\mapsto v_Sb$ identifies $e_SU$ with the right regular $H_d(\mathbf a)$-module. Put $A=\operatorname{End}_{H_d(\mathbf a)}U$. Since $e_SU$ is regular, $Ae_S=\operatorname{Hom}_{H_d}(e_SU,U)\cong U$ by evaluation at $v_S$. Consequently $h:H_d(\mathbf a)\to e_SAe_S$, characterized by $h(b)v_S=v_Sb$, is an algebra isomorphism, and $\theta\mapsto\theta(v_S)$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{A}(U,M)$ with $e_SM$ for every finite-image module $M$. The left Hecke action on this corner is $h$, not the naive right action on $M$. [F3, F5, construct, algebra]

2.1 **The cyclic symmetric generator and its bottom quotient.** Write $A-A_c=(a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ and form the actual cumulative-column $\mathfrak p$-module $Z=\bigotimes_i\operatorname{Sym}^{a_i}(V_{\le\operatorname{col}(i)})$. Its bottom column degree is $b=\sum_i a_i(l-\operatorname{col}(i))$; the higher-degree part is a $\mathfrak p$-submodule, and $Z/Z_{>b}$ is the inflated Levi module $Z_b=\bigotimes_j\bigotimes_r\operatorname{Sym}^{\mu_r^{(j)}}(E_j)$. Put $w_A=\sum_{w\in\prod_iS_{a_i}}w$ and $x_A=\prod_i\prod_{k=1}^{a_i}\prod_{j>\operatorname{col}(i)}(x_{a_1+\cdots+a_{i-1}+k}-a_j)$. Apply these factors in order starting with the first tensor place. The actual dot formula gives $v_Sx_A=v_{\mathbf j}$, where $\mathbf j$ has the ordered rows of $v_S$ and column sequence prescribed by $A-A_c$; subtracting $a_j$ cancels the scalar at column $j$ and moves that box one column left. Hence $v_Sx_Aw_A=v_{\mathbf j}w_A\in e_SZ$. More generally the vectors $v_Swx_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}x_Aw_A$, with $0\le r_k<\operatorname{col}(\mathbf j_k)$ and $w$ ranging over cosets of $\prod_i S_{a_i}$, have distinct leading symmetrized tensors and span $e_SZ$ by the ordinary symmetric-tensor basis. Thus this vector generates $e_SZ$ as a corner module, and its image generates $e_S(Z/Z_{>b})$. These are actual vector identities and triangular basis statements, rather than a character identification. [F1, F3, F5, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 **The affine colour fibre.** Ordinary Levi Schur-Weyl gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak h}(U,Z_b)\cong\bigotimes_j M^{\mu^{(j)}}$ on the canonical colour fibre, where $M^{\mu}$ is the symmetric-group permutation module. Its vectors in the corner are $v_{\mathbf j}ww_A+e_SZ_{>b}$ with $w\in S_{d_1}\times\cdots\times S_{d_l}$. For $k=d_1+\cdots+d_{j-1}+1$, the identity $v_{\mathbf j}=v_Sx_A$ and commutativity of dots give $h(x_k)v_{\mathbf j}ww_A=v_Sx_Ax_kww_A=v_{\mathbf j}x_kww_A$. In the bottom quotient the dot formula has scalar $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$: its left-neighbour term has higher degree, all preceding places have strictly smaller column and all later places have greater or equal column, so both signed transposition sums are empty. Thus $x_k$ acts as $a_j$ on that canonical fibre. The affine cross relations then determine the remaining dots as $a_j$ plus their within-block Jucys-Murphy sums. This proves that the fibre inclusion is a homomorphism for the affine Young subalgebra $H_{d_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{d_l}$, with module $\bigotimes_j\mathrm{ev}_{a_j}^*M^{\mu^{(j)}}$, and its image generates the entire corner by step 2.1. [F3, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 **The genuine Specht isomorphism.** The Levi Young-symmetrizer map gives an actual quotient $Z_b\twoheadrightarrow V(A)$ and hence a $\mathfrak p$-quotient $Z/Z_{>b}\twoheadrightarrow V(A)$. The canonical colour fibre quotient is $\bigotimes_j S^{\mu^{(j)}}$, by ordinary Levi Schur-Weyl. The affine fibre map in step 3.1 descends through this actual quotient and still generates: $e_S$ is exact and the generating vector of its source maps onto a generator of its quotient. Affine induction therefore gives a surjection $S(A)\twoheadrightarrow e_SV(A)$. The multilinear row-weight part of $\bigotimes_j S_{\mu^{(j)}}(E_j)$ has one summand for each allocation of the $d$ distinct rows into ordered colour subsets of sizes $d_j$, and on each subset its weight space is the polytabloid Specht space. Its dimension is $d!/(d_1!\cdots d_l!)\prod_j\dim S^{\mu^{(j)}}$. This is also the induced module's dimension, since the affine algebra is free over its affine Young subalgebra with the finite shuffle basis. The existing surjection is therefore an isomorphism. Steps 1.1 and [F2] identify its target with $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U,V(A))=\pi(N(A))$, preserving the actual Hecke maps. [F1, F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 **Descent to the original pyramid.** Extend the original label $A$ by the added ground rows, producing a contractible large label $A^+$. Its column partitions $\mu^{(j)}$ and roots $a_j$ are unchanged. The actual original-path/zero-occupancy compression in [F3] gives $eV(A^+)=V(A)$ and $eU^+=U$, with the faithful supporting-block Morita equivalence and natural Hom comparison. Every simple constituent of $V(A^+)$ has the same entry-multiset central character as $A^+$; the bottom-row minimum argument forces every such label to be contractible. Hence the supporting central idempotent satisfies $fV(A^+)=V(A^+)$, and the Hom comparison identifies the original $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U,V(A))$ with the entire large Hom module, rather than an arbitrary quotient of it. Step 4.1 therefore descends the same intrinsic Specht isomorphism to the original pyramid. [F3, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 Tilting images and full faithfulness. The opposite-parabolic flag coefficients are the actual tilting-character coefficients of [F1] and [F4]; exact $\pi$ carries each successive standard section to its Specht module by steps 4.1–5.1, so it preserves these flag multiplicities. For fullness, the local corner proof of [F2] applies: in the finite summand algebra $A$, $\pi$ is equivalent to $e(-)$ and has right adjoint $G(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{eAe}(eA,X)$. Its unit on a target with standard socle is injective and has off-standard cokernel. A tilting has standard socle from its standard flag and standard head from its costandard flag and simple-preserving restricted duality. Any map from it to the off-standard cokernel vanishes, since a nonzero quotient would have standard head. Adjunction therefore factors every map between its Schur images uniquely through the original target, proving full faithfulness on tiltings. [F1, F2, F4, step 5.1, algebra]

6.2 Simple images and heads. The finite-W simple-image classification and the genuine Morita equivalence in [F2] and [F3] imply that $D(A)=\pi(L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))$ is simple for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, that these are distinct and exhaustive, and that $\pi(L(A))=0$ otherwise. For a standard label $A$, the cover $P(A)$ is an indecomposable summand of $T$, so $Y(A)=\pi(P(A))$ is an indecomposable projective. Its simple quotients are determined by $\operatorname{Hom}_{B_d}(Y(A),D(B))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(P(A),L(B))$, which has dimension $\delta_{A,B}$; this is the ordinary equivalence on $\operatorname{add}(T)$ and the simple-image computation. Thus $Y(A)$ has head $D(A)$. Lift the cover $P(A)\to L(A)$ through $N(A)\to L(A)$ using projectivity; the lift is surjective since the latter is the simple-head quotient and any proper submodule of $N(A)$ lies in its radical. Exactness yields $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow S(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$. Every nonzero quotient of the indecomposable projective $Y(A)$ has the same simple head $D(A)$: its kernel is contained in the unique maximal submodule. Therefore $S(A)$ has head $D(A)$. [F1, F2, F3, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Projective images. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, the preceding step shows that $Y(A)=\pi(P(A))$ is the indecomposable projective with simple head $D(A)$, hence its projective cover. Evaluation $T\otimes_{B_d}\pi(P(A))\to P(A)$ is an isomorphism because $P(A)\in\operatorname{add}(T)$: this is checked on $T$ and restricted to its idempotent summands. Thus $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$. Off-standard projectives retain their actual images, and no projective-preservation assertion follows for them. [F2, step 6.2, algebra]

8.1 Multiplicities. Since $\pi$ is exact and its kernel is generated by the off-standard simples, the composition multiplicities of $S(A)=\pi(N(A))$ are the multiplicities of the simple $L(B)$ in $N(A)$ for $B\in\mathrm{Std}$; by the Fock-space dictionary [F4] the typed coefficient of the dual-canonical/canonical pairing equals $d_{B,A}(1)$, so $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$; for $B\notin\mathrm{Std}$ the module $D(B)$ is zero and is not a simple Hecke label. All the identifications above are ungraded and taken at parameter $1$. [F2, F4, step 6.2, algebra] ∎

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For admissible origins $c$ the genuine Whittaker functor $V$ of
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]] is exact
on $\mathcal O_c^d$, and
$$\gamma\colon\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{W}(V_c^{\otimes d},V(-))$$
is a natural isomorphism, where $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Both $V$ and the
Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ are fully faithful on
all projective objects of the relevant summand, and the quotient is also fully
faithful on tiltings. $T$ is a self-dual prinjective detecting object
containing all standard-labelled projective-injective covers, each individually self-dual, but it need not be a
generator of the entire category-$\mathcal O$ summand. $V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$
is a projective generator of $W_d$-mod, and $V$ preserves projectivity on
$\operatorname{add}(T)$; it need not send every projective of $\mathcal O$ to
a projective $W$-module. The composite of $V$ with the Morita equivalence is
the Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples.

[F1] The genuine continuous-dual Whittaker construction is exact, sends $N(A)$ to its finite-Levi $W$-standard, kills precisely off-$\mathrm{Std}$ simples, and has a coherent bimodule isomorphism $j:V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}(T)\to U$. Its independent filtered loop/Vust construction proves the raw mutual centralizers before this factorization; stable faithfulness is established directly in step 11.1 below. Its actual tensor maps intertwine Casimir operators and crossings, including tensoring by the distinct contragredient $V^*$; its exact faithful factor through the corner has the form $U\otimes_B-$ and is Morita. These are the local original-head/right-normalizer, continuous-dual, tensor and Nakayama constructions of [[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]]. No simple-image classification is assumed before the factor/progenerator calculation there.

[F4] The cyclotomic algebra has its bounded PBW basis and symmetric top-coefficient trace, nondegenerate on every central block corner ([[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]). The actual row-weight operators on tensor space and the Casimir formula are those of [[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]; original path and Gauss coefficient expansions are [[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. The finite-Levi standard has its entry-multiset scalar central character. Restricted transpose duality has a nondegenerate form on $P_c$ and on $V$, so their tensor product supplies $T\cong DT$, with the Casimir and crossings self-adjoint. This is transposition duality, not an assertion $V^*=V$.

3.1 **The detector and the injective hulls it contains.** The ground simple is projective-injective. Tensoring by $V$ preserves both projectives and injectives because the distinct tensor functor $-\otimes V^*$ is exact and adjoint on both sides. The tensor product contravariant form gives $T\cong DT$. Every simple submodule of a standard-filtered object embeds in one of its successive standard sections, by taking the first section meeting it; hence step 2.1 proves standard socle for every projective and for $T$. Duality gives standard head for $T$. Every standard label of positive degree is $\widetilde f_iB$ for a lower-degree standard label by [F3]; induction using the actual crystal head of $f_iL(B)$ gives $T\twoheadrightarrow L(A)$. Lift this epimorphism through $P(A)\twoheadrightarrow L(A)$; essentiality makes the lift surjective and projectivity splits it. Thus the indecomposable summands of $T$ are exactly the standard-labelled covers, all with positive multiplicity and all injective. Moreover $I(A)=DP(A)\in\operatorname{add}(DT)=\operatorname{add}(T)$ for every standard $A$. This hull membership does not presume individual summand self-duality. [F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

8.1 **The actual Whittaker comparison and quotient.** By [F1] the exact Whittaker functor factors through $F$ as the actual equivalence $U\otimes_B-$, with $U$ a right $B$-progenerator and $W_d=\operatorname{End}_B(U)$. Its inverse is $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U,-)$, and its unit on $FX$ is $m\mapsto(u\mapsto u\otimes m)$. Under the source action this is precisely $\gamma_X(f)=V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}(f)j^{-1}$, since the counit on $T\otimes_B FX$ is evaluation; thus the comparison is a natural isomorphism of actual maps and Hecke modules. In particular $U$ is a left $W_d$-progenerator, and $V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}$ is fully faithful on projectives by step 6.1. The corner functor $F$ is the Serre quotient with kernel consisting of objects with only off-standard factors; applying the genuine equivalence identifies the same quotient for $V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}$. Projectivity is preserved on $\operatorname{add}(T)$, whose image consists of the corresponding projective covers. This does not assert preservation for other ambient projectives. [F1, step 3.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, construct, algebra]

9.1 **Simple images and standard heads.** The exact corner functor kills precisely off-standard simples and identifies its other simple images with the distinct exhaustive $B$-simples; the genuine equivalence of step 8.1 transports these to the corresponding finite-W simples $L_W(A)$. For standard $A$, $P(A)\in\operatorname{add}(T)$, so $\pi P(A)$ is an indecomposable $B$-projective with head $\pi L(A)$: its Hom to each simple is the corresponding Hom from $P(A)$ by the elementary add$(T)$ equivalence. Lift $P(A)\to L(A)$ through $N(A)\to L(A)$; the image surjects onto the standard's head and is therefore the whole standard. Applying exact $\pi$ makes $\pi N(A)$ a nonzero quotient of this indecomposable projective, so it has the same unique simple head. Through Morita, the actual finite-Levi standard $V(A)=V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}N(A)$ likewise has unique simple head $L_W(A)$. This does not assert that a specified finite-Levi highest vector generates it. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 8.1, algebra]

9.2 **Independent row compression.** Add $t$ full ground rows until the enlarged smallest column has height at least $d$; all roots $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ remain fixed. For each row $r$, the normalized coefficient $D_r^{(1)}$ is its row-Cartan operator, with ground scalar $\kappa_r=\sum_{j:\,r\text{ lies in column }j}c_j$. On the actual tensor space and every finite-Levi standard of degree $d$ its eigenvalues are $\kappa_r+h$, $0\le h\le d$, since the remaining weight is polynomial row occupancy. Thus the SAME finite-image element $e=\prod_{r\text{ deleted}}\prod_{h=1}^{d}(1-(D_r^{(1)}-\kappa_r)/h)$ is the zero-deleted-occupancy projector on both tensor space and all these standards. In $U^+$ it selects tensors using only retained rows. The actual dot formula preserves row multisets, so $e$ commutes with dots and crossings and belongs to the left image by the independent raw first centralizer of [F1]. Each right matrix restricts identically under the retained-box embedding: left neighbours and row/column indices agree and its scalar $a_j$ is unchanged. Therefore $eU^+=U$ as right Hecke modules. Extending a commuting endomorphism of $eU^+$ by zero shows $eA^+e=A$, where $A^+,A$ are the large and small left image algebras. For the finite-Levi standard, the zero-deleted-occupancy part of $\mathbb C_{c_j}\otimes S_{\mu^{(j)}}(\mathbb C^{q_j+t})$ is $\mathbb C_{c_j}\otimes S_{\mu^{(j)}}(\mathbb C^{q_j})$ by its tensor Young-symmetrizer realization, and vanishes exactly when a deleted-row partition entry is nonzero. In the original path expansion, Levi projection kills off-column factors and each surviving strictly-forward path has at most one factor in each column. A deleted intermediate row changes removed-coordinate occupancy in a column with no later factor there to undo it; compression therefore kills that monomial. Remaining paths are exactly the small paths. The head shift in column $j$ changes by $-(j-1)t$, cancelling the retained source-reading shift $+(j-1)t$; its normalized highest weight remains the entry plus row index minus one. The corner action and its Gauss coefficients consequently give $eV(A^+)=V(A)$ for contractible labels and zero for noncontractible labels, as actual module identifications. [F1, F2, F4, step 8.1, construct, algebra]

10.1 **Simple contraction without highest-vector assumptions.** Every noncontractible standard simple is killed by $e$, because it is a quotient of the standard annihilated in step 9.2. For a finite algebra and an idempotent $e$, restriction gives a bijection between its simple modules surviving $e$ and the simples of $eAe$: any nonzero vector in $eL$ generates $eL=eAe v$, and for a small simple $M$ the module $Ae\otimes_{eAe}M$ has a unique simple quotient surviving $e$. Indeed its $e$-part is $M$; every proper submodule has zero $e$-part, since a submodule containing that part generates the whole induced module. The sum of all such proper submodules is still annihilated by $e$ and is the unique maximal submodule. Apply this to the independent corner in step 9.2. By step 9.1 both simple lists are complete, and small standard labels are in bijection with contractible large standard labels by adjoining full ground rows. Thus the survivors form a subset of the contractible list with exactly the same finite cardinality, so every contractible simple survives. Its restriction is a simple quotient of $eV(A^+)=V(A)$, which has the unique head from step 9.1, hence $eL_W(A^+)=L_W(A)$. [F1, step 9.1, step 9.2, construct, algebra]

11.1 **Fullness and the central Hecke corner.** If a contractible $A^+$ and another label have the same entry-multiset central character, admissibility separates charge cosets and identifies all charges within each coset. Its minimal bottom entry $c_j+1-(n+t)$ appears in each column of that coset; strictness and nonnegative ground differences force the same entries into the bottom row of the other label. Remove that row and repeat for every deleted row. Thus the contractible labels form a union of whole central-character blocks. Let $f$ be their central support in $A^+$; then $e=ef=fe$, since $e$ kills all complementary simples. Every simple of $A_f=fA^+f$ survives $e$ by step 10.1. If $A_feA_f$ were proper, its nonzero quotient would have a simple killed by $e$, a contradiction. Hence $f=\sum_k a_keb_k$. Multiplication $A_fe\otimes_{eA_fe}eM\to M$ has inverse $m\mapsto\sum_k a_ke\otimes eb_km$; balancing and this identity verify both composites. This gives a faithful Morita equivalence on all supported-block modules. The operator $f$ belongs to the right centralizer and is central there, so restriction identifies $fB^+f=\operatorname{End}_{A_f}(fU^+)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $B=\operatorname{End}_{eA_fe}(eU^+)^{\mathrm{op}}$. To verify enlarged stable faithfulness directly, choose $d$ distinct terminal boxes on length-$l$ Jordan strings. In the associated graded tensor action each bounded PBW word $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_d^{a_d}w$, $0\le a_i<l$, sends their ordered terminal tensor to the tensor in which those distinct strings have been permuted by $w$ and the box on string $i$ moved $a_i$ places left. These $l^dd!$ outputs are distinct basis tensors, so the graded PBW word images are linearly independent. A nonzero filtered Hecke element has a nonzero leading PBW symbol; graded injectivity makes its leading operator nonzero, hence its actual operator is nonzero. The enlarged stable action is therefore faithful, giving $B=fH_d(\mathbf a)f$. Its trace is therefore symmetric and nondegenerate by [F4]. This local proof precedes, and does not depend on, a later stable-range definition. [F1, F2, F4, step 9.2, step 10.1, construct, algebra]

Put $\delta M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,T)$ with $(bf)(m)=f(m)b^*$, and $X^\#=\operatorname{Hom}_{B}(X,B)$ with the same twist. Transposition gives the natural isomorphism $\delta M\to\pi DM$, $f\mapsto Df\circ\beta$, whose inverse is $g\mapsto\beta^{-1}\circ Dg\circ\operatorname{bidual}_M$. This uses only $T\cong DT$, not individual projective self-duality. Tensor-Hom gives $\delta\pi^*\cong\#$, and the symmetric trace of step 11.1 gives $\#\cong D_B$ by $h\mapsto\operatorname{tr}\circ h$. Define $\theta_M:M\to D\pi^*\delta M$ by $\theta_M(m)(t\otimes f)=(t,f(m))$. The form identity $(xtb,t')=(t,x^{\mathrm{tr}}t'b^*)$ makes this balanced and $\mathfrak g$-linear. Applying $\pi$ gives a natural map $\pi\to\pi D\pi^*\delta\cong\#\pi D$ between exact functors; exactness of $\#$ follows from the symmetric algebra's injective regular module. On $T$ it is the regular trace-duality isomorphism, and hence is invertible on add$(T)$. Use the copresentations of step 5.1 and kernels to prove it invertible on every projective; use finite projective presentations and cokernels to prove it invertible on every object. Dualizing gives the genuine module isomorphism $\pi D\cong D_B\pi$. [F2, F4, step 5.1, step 11.1, construct, algebra]

Assume the bounded-below setting of the tower: $I\subseteq\mathbb Z$ is nonempty,
consecutive and bounded below, $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ is an admitted integral
multicharge, and $H^\Lambda=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q^+}H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the
degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower of

standard, tableaux of the Fock data of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]], with monomials $M_A$ and
dual-canonical vectors $L_A$, canonical vectors $T_A$ and quasi-canonical vectors
$P_A$ as in [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], and
let $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}$ be the normalized highest projection, so that
$D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$ and $S_B=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B$. Work at source
parameter $s=1$.

**(i)** The exact Schur quotient identifies the module Grothendieck group
$G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ with the FULL integral costandard lattice
$$V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{\,D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A\ :\ A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\,\}$$
by $[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, and it sends every Specht class to
$[S(B)]\mapsto S_B=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B$; the vectors
$\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ are another integral basis, the standard
monomial basis.

**(ii)** The endomorphisms of $G_0$ induced by the residue functors $e_i,f_i$
$(i\in I)$ are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ of the integrable
$\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock action, and both the standard and the costandard
integral forms carry the actual divided-power action.

**(iii)** Over $\mathbb Q$ the ground class generates the dual highest weight
module $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$. Over $\mathbb Z$ the costandard lattice need
NOT be ground cyclic, even under divided powers: the rank-one case
$I=\{0\}$, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$ has a ground-generated integral lattice of
index two that omits $D_{01}$. The STANDARD lattice, by contrast, is integrally
generated by its ground vector under divided powers.

**(iv)** Every standard-tableau simple occurs as a composition factor of a
residue word applied to the ground simple, and the ground crystal component is
exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$.

**(v)** The categorical reachability and rational-cyclicity statements of
(iii)-(iv) do not imply integral costandard cyclicity; the level-$0$ tower has
only the ground weight.

For an arbitrary admitted consecutive $I$, the same statements hold blockwise and sum to the same lattice identifications. Use finite letter cuts containing every charge and finite root cuts containing the selected content and every intermediate content in the chosen residue words. The transition maps append the common ground tail below the lower cut and leave all letters above the upper cut absent. They fix the intrinsic Hecke generators, spectral idempotents and residue bimodules on the selected contents, and identify both integral lattices by their labelled bases. Assume the bounded-below setting, the tower $H^\Lambda$ and its residue functors of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], and the Fock data
with the four bases of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]].
For $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ let $D(A)$ be the simple module of the
identification of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
and let $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$ be its projective cover in
$\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$. Work at source parameter $s=1$.

**(ii)** Under the identifications (i) and
[[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
the map $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\to G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ induced
by the embedding of projectives into all finite-dimensional modules is the
natural injective inclusion $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$
of the standard lattice into the full costandard lattice.

**(iv)** Both residue functors $e_i$ and $f_i$ on projective modules induce
operators on $K_0$ that are the Chevalley operators adjoint to their $G_0$
operators of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]].

**Given:** The inherited Axiom of Choice and the tower $H^\Lambda$ and its block-wise Grothendieck groups as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], the exact Schur
quotient $\pi$ with right-exact left adjoint $\pi^*$ of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]], the
Schur-image identifications $\pi(N(A))=S(A)$, $\pi(L(A))=D(A)$,
$\pi(P(A))=Y(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and
$\pi^*\pi(P(A))=P(A)$ of
[[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]],
and the Fock dictionary $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}(P_A)=P_A$, $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_B=D_B$
at parameter one. We prove (i)-(v).

1.1 **The split $K_0$ basis of covers.** Every simple finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda$-module has a projective cover, unique up to isomorphism, and the classes $[Y(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, of the covers of the simples $D(A)$ of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the split Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective modules; this is [F1] applied block by block and summed over $\alpha\in Q^+$. [F1, given, construct]

1.2 **The left adjoint on projectives.** The Schur quotient $\pi$ has a left adjoint $\pi^*$ which is right exact on all modules and sends $H$-projectives to category-O projectives; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ one has $\pi^*(Y(A))=P(A)$ and $\pi\pi^*(Y(A))=Y(A)$, so $\pi^*$ recovers the standard-labelled prinjectives, and its exactness on arbitrary modules is not needed. These are the statements of [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]]. [given, construct]

3.1 **The inclusion is the lattice inclusion.** The embedding of projectives into all finite-dimensional modules induces a map on Grothendieck groups; in the category of finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda$-modules a projective class $[Y(A)]$ maps to the class of the same module, which under the identification $\Phi$ of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] is the costandard coordinate vector of the module $Y(A)$. By step 1.2, $\pi\pi^*(Y(A))=Y(A)$, so this vector equals the image of $[P(A)]$ under the exact quotient, namely $P_A$ by step 1.3. Hence the composite $\Phi\circ(\text{inclusion})\circ\Psi^{-1}$ is the identity on the basis $\{P_A\}$, i.e. the natural inclusion $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$. It is injective because the vectors $P_A$ are linearly independent in the rational highest module, and hence also as elements of its full costandard lattice. The normalized highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space; no claim that the embedded standard and costandard lattices coincide is used. This proves (ii). [step 1.3, step 2.1, given, algebra]

3.2 **The Cartan pairing is the normalized highest pairing.** By [F2] the Cartan pairing descends to $K_0\times G_0$ and pairs the two bases dually; under the identifications of step 2.1 and of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] the value on basis vectors is computed on the Fock side, where the pairing between the standard and costandard families at parameter one is the normalized highest pairing $C_0$ with $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ by [[lem-the-fock-pairing-matches-projective-simple-and-standard-costandard-pairings]]. This proves (iii); in particular the costandard vectors entering the pairing are the projected simples $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_B=D_B$, not unprojected monomials. [step 2.1, F2, given, algebra]

5.1 **The full integral extension.** The arbitrary-$I$ construction of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] fixes each selected finite-dimensional algebra $H_\alpha^\Lambda$, its simple labels and residue bimodules. An algebra identity fixes projective covers of the identified simples, uniquely up to isomorphism, so it fixes their split-$K_0$ basis. The lower lattice map is $P_A\mapsto P_{\jmath A}$ under the same common-ground-tail label map; the actual lower/global cut compatibility makes this an integral basis identification commuting with divided powers and with the pairing against the full upper basis. It therefore transports $\Psi$, the Cartan map and its pairing on each content; overlaps agree by the intrinsic algebra identity and the composable tail maps. Their weightwise direct sum proves (i)–(iv) for every admitted consecutive $I$, without claiming integral ground cyclicity for the costandard lattice. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, given, construct, algebra]
